title: The 5 Heaviest Stones Ever Moved by Muscle, Ranked (#1 Isn't Ancient)

scenes.text: The five heaviest stones ever moved by muscle alone. Number one isn't even ancient.

scenes.label: Alexander Column · ~600 tons
scenes.text: Number five: Russia's Alexander Column. About six hundred tons of granite, held up only by its own weight.

scenes.label: Colossi of Memnon · 720 tons
scenes.text: Number four: the Colossi of Memnon in Egypt. 720 tons each, hauled hundreds of kilometers 3,400 years ago.

scenes.label: Baalbek trilithon · ~800 tons
scenes.text: Number three: the Baalbek trilithon in Lebanon. Three Roman blocks, close to eight hundred tons apiece, nineteen meters long.

scenes.label: Ramesses colossus · 1,000 tons
scenes.text: Number two: the colossus of Ramesses the Second. Roughly a thousand tons of red granite, once twenty meters tall.

scenes.label: Thunder Stone · 1,500 tons
scenes.text: Number one: Russia's Thunder Stone. About 1,500 tons, hauled six kilometers by 400 men over nine months, in the eighteenth century. Today it's a statue's pedestal.

description:
The five heaviest single stones ever moved by human power, ranked by weight.
Guinness lists the Thunder Stone, the pedestal of the Bronze Horseman in St Petersburg, as the largest stone moved by manpower alone: about 1,500 tonnes, hauled 6 km by 400 men over nine months (it was cut down to about 1,250 tonnes on the way). The fallen colossus of Ramesses II at the Ramesseum weighed roughly 1,000 tons; the three trilithon blocks at Baalbek are 750 to 800 tonnes each; the Colossi of Memnon about 720 tons each; and the Alexander Column about 600 tonnes. Bigger stones exist at Baalbek and Aswan, but they never left the quarry.
Which one would you have least wanted to pull?
first_comment: The Thunder Stone rolled on bronze balls about six inches wide, over just 100 metres of reusable track. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
